title: Implement permanent PostgreSQL ledger storage and host payload conformance
summary: Provide a neutral PostgreSQL implementation of Storage and shared conformance for host-backed PayloadStore implementations so StateCivics can keep Matter's ledger and payload recovery in its existing database infrastructure. Decision 0003 makes both ports prerequisites for StateCivics production activation: no interim production mount or temporary deployment/file-backup plumbing. Retain SQLite and the existing rehearsal for comparison and verification. StateCivics owns its packet/response adapter, receiving integration and activation; this ticket owns the Matter SDK work only.
in_scope: A synchronous PostgreSQL Storage implementation opened through a host-supplied psycopg connection factory or pool lease, with explicit transaction ownership, connection cleanup and scope isolation.

Equivalent canonical history, command idempotency, revision checks, consistent snapshots, historical proof reads, guarded retries, dependency watches, transaction hooks and uncertain-outcome handling.
Database coordination that protects absent records and competing discoveries, plus an explicit host contract preserving per-place and per-lens review exclusion across separate commands.
Reusable PayloadStore conformance and a synthetic host adapter fixture covering durable exact-byte put/read, packet reconstruction, raw response artifacts and availability/access boundaries.
Versioned PostgreSQL migrations, integrity verification, actual restore checks, SDK compatibility guidance and installed-package evidence, reusing the existing SQLite behavioral scenarios.
out_of_scope: Interim production data/matter mounts, MATTER_STORE_ROOT directory rollout, temporary file-backup/deployment plumbing or activating SQLite first.

Editing or deploying StateCivics, Oil, the crawler or DIAT; StateCivics KS-1158 owns its host payload tables/adapter, schema/place layout, backend/worker coordination and associated storage recovery/receiving acceptance. Encryption remains KS-637/KS-1152 work; the production dispatcher (KS-1127) and activation remain separate StateCivics/owner work.
Replacing StateCivics evidence, client, assistant/session or retrieval infrastructure, or adding civic concepts to the neutral Storage or PayloadStore protocols.
Changing frozen monitoring/review wire contracts, record meanings, access rules, provider qualification or production activation authority.
Generic retention/archival expansion under MAT-073, removal of SQLite, copying real rehearsal data into this repository, or presuming a live production SQLite migration is needed.
implementation: Inspect Storage, Snapshot, Transaction, SQLiteStore, PayloadStore, GuardedStorage, the dependency observer and existing storage tests; map each observable guarantee to the second backend rather than copying SQLite-specific SQL or replacing existing host infrastructure.

Define the synchronous psycopg factory/lease boundary, supported PostgreSQL/driver versions and host-selected schema/scope isolation. Specify transaction ownership, durable-return semantics, nested-use refusal, rollback/lease cleanup and bounded lock waits; never silently commit unrelated host work.

Implement append-only canonical versions and command results, heads, watches and migrations with the existing identity/revision constraints. Preserve exact bytes for hashes rather than relying on database JSON reserialization. Keep optional PostgreSQL dependencies from breaking SQLite-only imports/installations.

Implement consistent snapshots and guarded current/historical reads, replay disclosure and per-scope coordination for absent reads and competing identity/watch creation. Retain current control/access fences and logical lens exclusion; external model or assistant calls remain outside database transactions.

Preserve handler savepoints, failure journaling, observer timing and rollback, and post-commit hook semantics. Inject failures before/during/after commit and reconcile uncertain outcomes through exact command identities without automatic handler or assistant retries.

Exercise PayloadStore with a synthetic host fixture: resolve an authorized packet row by packet_hash, reconstruct exact_material with canonical_bytes and derive/verify source_digest and byte length. evidence_hash hashes the packet identity object, not the payload; retain/derive a scoped payload-digest-to-packet association. Exercise durable host-owned raw response artifacts separately and explicit missing/withheld/corrupt outcomes.

Adapt shared behavioral tests to both backends, with real PostgreSQL process concurrency and fault cases. Verify migrations and a restore into a new target including payload/artifact recovery, exact retries, pending pressure and unknown wakes. Keep the existing SQLite rehearsal intact; any later authorized import must preserve exact identities and evidence.

Publish a compatibility/recovery matrix and receiving guide for KS-1158, including SDK/image and ledger/payload recovery pins. Record actual Matter source/synthetic/PostgreSQL evidence separately from StateCivics connected receiving and provider/live-use evidence; do not mark production activation ready from this ticket alone.

acceptance.criterion: A host-supplied synchronous connection factory or pool lease supports the existing Storage API with explicit transaction ownership, scope isolation and durable successful returns; SQLite-only consumers remain usable.
acceptance.verification: Run installed-package cases with and without the optional PostgreSQL dependency, independent scopes and reused pool leases; reject unsupported/nested transaction usage and verify cleanup after both success and failure without changing unrelated host transactions.

acceptance.criterion: Canonical versions, heads, watches, command/result bytes and receipts commit atomically; exact retries return the original result, changed content conflicts, and immutable identity/history remains intact.
acceptance.verification: Run the existing transaction, boundary and identity scenarios against SQLite and real PostgreSQL; compare canonical bytes/digests and public outcomes across restart, changed retries, type collisions, stale writes and corrupted stored data.

acceptance.criterion: Competing writers cannot both win incompatible existing or absent-record decisions; watch registration and discovery races are protected, and host coordination preserves one active review per logical lens.
acceptance.verification: Use independent PostgreSQL connections/processes for missing-identity creation, expected-revision and negative-watch races, plus synthetic backend/worker claim races across lens revisions and matters. Assert one eligible winner, honest conflicts, bounded lock failures and safe release; a row-lock-only case must not pass by avoiding the absent-record race.

acceptance.criterion: Snapshots are consistent and historical proof reads retain their current-head fence; replay of a durable result cannot bypass present access, revocation or scope checks.
acceptance.verification: Race a writer against a multi-read snapshot; test historical pins with a changed current head, foreign scopes, revoked read/egress grants and exact retry disclosure through GuardedStorage. Assert explicit refusal without rewriting the historical command or result.

acceptance.criterion: Transaction observers and post-commit effects preserve their timing; refusals and unexpected exceptions have the existing rollback behavior, and uncertain commits do not authorize blind retries or duplicate external work.
acceptance.verification: Inject handler refusal, observer refusal/exception, connection loss and commit-acknowledgment loss. Check child-write rollback, correct failure journal or full rollback, no premature post-commit effect and exact-command reconciliation without a second handler/assistant invocation after a committed outcome.

acceptance.criterion: A conforming host payload adapter durably publishes and returns exact authorized bytes without a filesystem dependency, using the corrected packet mapping and preserving explicit availability and integrity failures.
acceptance.verification: In a synthetic host fixture, locate by packet_hash and reconstruct canonical_bytes(exact_material); compare source_digest and byte length with Matter's content reference. Include unequal evidence_hash/payload digest, shared material, missing/changed/foreign/withheld packets, an interrupted put and exact raw response recovery. Prove the digest-only read route can resolve its scoped packet association and cannot treat identity hashes as payload hashes.

acceptance.criterion: Versioned migrations and actual PostgreSQL restore verification recover the ledger together with its payload/artifact dependencies, including pending pressure and unresolved wakes, without fabricating completed or quiet work.
acceptance.verification: Exercise interrupted migrations, checksum/corruption refusals and a real dump/restore into a separate PostgreSQL target with synthetic host payload/artifact rows. Verify canonical histories, heads, watches, exact retries, pending pressure and unknown claims; missing payloads remain explicit. Row counts or schema checksums alone are insufficient.

acceptance.criterion: The SDK compatibility and recovery contract preserves supported stored meanings and the SQLite reference, refuses unsupported versions and requires compatible SDK/image, ledger and payload recovery pins.
acceptance.verification: Run supported and deliberately unsupported version fixtures, including dev20-era historical-context behavior and MAT-074 compatibility vectors, on the backend matrix. Document one-way boundaries and verify a compatible restored recovery set rather than claiming that an older image can read newer state.

acceptance.criterion: The receiving handoff names both permanent ports as StateCivics production prerequisites and assigns host payload implementation, coordination and storage recovery acceptance to KS-1158 without an interim production filesystem plan. Encryption remains KS-637/KS-1152 work; the production dispatcher and activation retain their separate StateCivics/owner scope.
acceptance.verification: Review the SDK guide and acceptance matrix against Decision 0003 and the pinned StateCivics request; identify executed Matter checks and still-required connected receiving evidence separately. Keep real rehearsal artifacts external and frozen wire/schema checks unchanged.

tests: Exact retry after restart or lost commit acknowledgment versus changed command content under the same key.
Absent identity and watch races between independent backend/worker connections, plus lens claims spanning different revisions and native matters.
Snapshot consistency, current-head-gated historical proofs and present revocation on replay disclosure.
Handler/observer rollback and post-commit timing under injected storage faults.
Packet identity hash differs from payload digest; reconstructed exact bytes, raw response artifacts, withheld reads and corrupt mappings remain distinguishable.
Restore of pending pressure, an unknown wake and all referenced payloads; missing bytes never become successful empty evidence.
Supported and unsupported SDK/schema combinations with SQLite comparison and optional dependency installation.
risks: PostgreSQL transaction isolation and locks are not interchangeable with SQLite's writer lock; absent reads and watch discovery require an explicit proof under real contention.
A pool lease or caller-owned transaction can accidentally expose uncommitted success, retain locks or commit unrelated host work unless ownership is enforced.
PayloadStore reads are digest-based while StateCivics packets are found by packet_hash; a missing scoped association or identity-hash substitution can break recovery or disclose foreign bytes.
Execution receipts and raw responses may contain client-sensitive material; database custody does not remove host access, encryption and recovery obligations.
A shared database does not make external assistant calls or host and Matter commits atomic; unknown wakes must retain their existing reconciliation controls.
Production activation waits for permanent storage and separately recorded host acceptance; SDK conformance alone is insufficient and no temporary production mount is authorized.

reuse.application: Implement the existing Storage/Snapshot/Transaction behavior and reuse SQLite as the comparison backend; keep civic and deployment meaning in the host.
Retain scoped exact-byte put/read, unframed source digests and durable response-artifact semantics; reuse the port rather than adding replacement evidence storage.
Preserve existing guarded retries, access/control fences, observer invalidation, lens exclusion and explicit unknown-wake reconciliation.
Adapt behavioral scenarios into a shared backend matrix; real PostgreSQL process/fault/restore evidence must supplement synthetic fixtures.
Reuse established owners and ports; this Matter ticket does not authorize downstream implementation or introduce replacement client, retrieval or orchestration infrastructure.

sources: Owner direction 2026-11-02: PostgreSQL ledger and host-backed payload persistence before production activation; no interim production mount or temporary deployment/file-backup plumbing; preserve the existing SQLite rehearsal.
